The 16-year-old Canó Jr. is set to be part of Miami's 2028 international signing class

        The Miami Marlins have reached a preliminary agreement with 16-year-old Robinson Canó Jr. that stands to make him part of the club's 2028 international signing class. The agreement is worth $1 million, reports Mike Rodriguez. MLB rules state that an international amateur free agent player is eligible to sign with an MLB organization between Jan. 15 and Dec. 15 of his signing class year. He must turn 17 before Sept. 1 of the year in which he signs. Canó Jr., a highly regarded shortstop out of the Dominican Republic who bats right-handed, is the son of former MLB great Robinson Canó. The elder Canó spent parts of 17 seasons in the majors, the majority of which came with the New York Yankees. Over that span, Canó earned eight All-Star selections and three Gold Gloves; racked up 2,639 hits and 335 home runs; and won a World Series ring as a member of the 2009 Yankees. He went on to sign a large free-agent contract with the Seattle Mariners, where he played from 2014-18. Canó's career total of 68.7 WAR would under normal circumstances make him a strong candidate for election to the Baseball Hall of Fame. However, two suspensions for positive PED tests make it unlikely he'll get a plaque, at least while he's on the BBWAA ballot. He last appeared in the majors in 2022 as a member of the Atlanta Braves.
Canó Jr. is also the grandson of José Canó, who appeared in the majors with the 1989 Houston Astros, which puts him in line to be a third-generation major leaguer.

body:
The Hurricanes are poised to sit atop the initial top 25 release on Tuesday, while a new metric could push a surprising SEC contender into the top four
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:00 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The first College Football Playoff Rankings of the 2026 season are finally almost here.On Tuesday night, the CFP Selection Committee will unveil its first rankings. Outside of the final rankings, the first are the most interesting because they establish a baseline for the rest of the season. There are new selection committee members (hello, Jeff Tedford and Gus Malzahn) and new metrics (strength of conference) that could lead to a new-look ranking from what we've seen in the past. It's why the first rankings are the hardest to predict because even when you know the metrics the committee focuses on, each group full of new members every year could prioritize some over others. CBS Sports has taken on the yeoman's work of predicting what the committee will do each week in its 1 through 25 rankings. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Miami (8-0)Best win: Wake ForestThe Hurricanes are the No. 1 team unless they lose. A win over Notre Dame this weekend would fortify this spot for Miami. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Georgia (7-1)Best win: AlabamaThe best team in the SEC should get a first-round bye if it wins the conference. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Utah (8-0)Best win: HoustonThe frontrunner to win the Big 12 could really solidify its position for a first-round bye with a win over BYU this weekend. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Kentucky (7-1)Best win: LSUKentucky has one of the best resumes in the country. The Wildcats are 2-1 against top-25 opponents, have the nation's No. 2 strength of record and No. 4 strength of schedule. Kentucky already has a marquee win over LSU and could bolster its case with a win over Tennessee on Saturday. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. BYU (7-1)Best win: Notre DameThe Cougars have both the best win (Notre Dame) and the worst loss (UCF) of the top five teams. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. UCLA (8-0)Best win: OregonWhere the Bruins land in the initial rankings will be one of the more fascinating decisions the committee makes. The Bruins have a weak schedule but are undefeated and poised to finish 11-1 or 12-0 in the regular season. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Indiana (8-1)Best win: NorthwesternNot only does Indiana have one of the weaker resumes, but the Hoosiers haven't passed the "eye test" in weeks. Indiana gets dinged for it in the first rankings. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Notre Dame (7-1)Best win: WisconsinAs I wrote over the weekend, ND's playoff path is suddenly perilous if it doesn't beat Miami this weekend. The Fighting Irish have no top-25 wins and won't even have a chance for one after Miami, with SMU getting knocked out of the top 25. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Texas (6-2)Best win: Ohio StateThe Longhorns get the edge over the Buckeyes with the head-to-head victory. Texas has two of the best wins in the country against a full-strength Ohio State and Ole Miss. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Alabama (6-2) Best win: KentuckyThe win over Kentucky has aged beautifully, and the two losses (Georgia, Tennessee) are both quality. There isn't much margin for error the rest of the way, though. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Ohio State (6-2)Best win: IndianaThe Buckeyes still have a 69.6% chance to make the playoff, according to the CBS Sports forecasting model, but that number drops to 36.3% if they lose to Oregon. Ohio State badly needs a win and to prove it is still a quality team without injured quarterback Julian Sayin. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Ole Miss (6-2)Best win: LSUThe Rebels have two quality wins (LSU, Missouri), one quality loss (Texas) and one blowout loss (Florida). This feels about right for Ole Miss, with the chance for a big jump next week if it can beat Georgia at home. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. Tennessee (6-2)Best win: AlabamaThe loss to South Carolina was damaging, but the win over Alabama is still valuable for the Vols' resume. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. Texas Tech (7-1)Best win: HoustonThe Red Raiders have a very manageable schedule down the stretch, which should allow them to move up the rankings in the future. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. USC (7-2)Best win: Ohio StateWith the smoke getting louder and louder about his job security, Lincoln Riley (briefly) quieted the critics with a win over Ohio State. It will be interesting, though, to see how much the committee discounts that win occurring against a Julian Sayin-less OSU team. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. Wake Forest (7-1)Best win: LouisvilleThis may feel low for the Demon Deacons, but zero top wins pulls them down a bit. There's room to move up, however, and its strong SOR rating (No. 10 nationally) will come in handy. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    17. LSU (6-2)Best win: AuburnThe Tigers have three big win opportunities coming up that will make or break their case– Alabama, Texas and Tennessee – but the resume is a bit lacking without a top-25 win. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    18. Missouri (6-2)Best win: FloridaA win over Texas this weekend could jump the Tigers into the top 10. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    19. Houston (6-2)Best win: Oklahoma StateThe Cougars have two quality losses (Utah, Texas Tech) but zero top 25 wins now that Oklahoma State dropped out. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    20. South Carolina (5-3)Best win: TennesseeThe Gamecocks yet again owned October with wins over Florida, Tennessee and Oklahoma. With a 2-2 record against the top 25 and SOR and SOS that rank in the top 25, South Carolina has a sneaky good resume. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    21. Florida (5-3)Best win: Ole MissThe Gators have two quality wins (Ole Miss, Texas), two bad blowout losses (Missouri, South Carolina) and one understandable loss (Georgia). 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    22. Iowa (6-2)Best win: Michigan The Hawkeyes blasted Wisconsin and are still hanging around, albeit a playoff longshot. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    23. Boise State (7-1)Best win: MemphisThe Broncos remain the highest-rated Group of Six school and would earn an automatic bid into the field. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    24. Oregon (5-3)Best win: USCThe Ducks' playoff hopes are hanging by a thread but would jump nearly 20% from 5.7 to 24.7% playoff odds with a road win over Ohio State on Saturday. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    25. Northwestern (6-2)Best win: Penn State This final spot came down to Northwestern and Arizona, but the Wildcats got the slight edge with better SOR and SOS ratings.

title: Tom Fornelli's College Football Power Ratings: Georgia and Miami remain on top, but cracks begin to show - CBS Sports
description: Georgia holds the top spot despite shaky quarterback play as the calendar turns to Nove
body:
Georgia holds the top spot despite shaky quarterback play as the calendar turns to November and the margin for error disappears for every national title contender
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:39 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Tensions are rising across the country, and not because it's election day. Well, OK, tensions are probably rising in parts of the country because of the elections, too. After all, every politician currently running is the most evil human being on the planet, according to the political ads that have been shown ad nauseam during college football games over the last two months.But I digress. While there's tension politically, there's as much tension in college football. It's one thing when the first couple of months of a season are crazy, as the 2026 season has been. It's new, it's exciting, and it's fun. But when the calendar flips to November, and you can see the end of the line off in the distance, that humor seems to disappear when your team is still in contention.Now it feels like the stakes are raised a bit, and any late-season loss could derail things in a way that September's slip-up didn't. You're also much more familiar with your team, and since every team in the country has a problem spot, you're much more aware of what it is now. And you know that, if it hasn't been fixed by now, it's not going to get fixed. You're scared that it's going to cost you at some point. In fact, you know it is; you just don't know when.Then you look at this Saturday's slate of games and realize, "Oh, it'll probably be this weekend." So, yeah, if you're feeling nervous or tense about your team right now. Don't worry. You're not alone. Maybe turn on some election coverage to distract yourself!
2025 Preseason Fornelli Power Ratings1
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Georgia
                    
    
    I've caught some heat from Georgia fans lately over my criticism of Gunner Stockton, but I'm only telling you what I've seen. He's been bad the last two games, even in this week's blowout win over Florida. It doesn't mean he won't get his act together down the stretch, but if Georgia wants to win a national title, it needs Stockton to perform better than he has against Auburn and Florida. You aren't winning three playoff games with performances like those from your QB unless your defense goes on a generational run.  Last Week: 1 | Title Odds: +3502
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Miami (Fla.)
                    
    
    So if you're a Miami fan, you're definitely getting a bit nervous about your defense right now. Miami didn't allow more than 20 points in any of its first five games this season, but has now allowed 35 to Florida State, 23 to a Pitt team with a backup QB and 35 to North Carolina. No offense to those three teams, but any offense the Hurricanes face in a playoff game will probably be better than those three. It's great that the offense continues to ball out, but you'd like to have the confidence in your defense to carry you in case that offense has an off day.  Last Week: 2 | Title Odds: +6203
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Notre Dame
                    
    
    Notre Dame did not escape the Navy game unscathed. Linebacker Drayk Bowen, the team's leading tackler, has already been ruled out of this week's game against Miami. Defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are questionable for the game, too. The timing is pretty awful, seeing how the Irish essentially have a two-game season, and they already lost the first leg. They might need that offense to have a good night against that struggling Miami defense.  Last Week: 4 | Title Odds: +5504
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Alabama
                    
    
    The greatest feeling in the world for a college football fan these days is to know your team has a bye week, because it means that your team won't be the one having a bad day this week. I hope Alabama enjoyed their time off as it prepares to hit the road to face LSU in one of four games between teams in this week's power ratings. There wasn't much change this week, but odds are we'll see some next week!  Last Week: 5 | Title Odds: +11005
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Ohio State
                    
    
    I'm not an anthropologist, but I have enjoyed studying the behavior of Ohio State fans since Saturday's loss to USC. They are in an extremely unfamiliar position, and they're acting like they have no idea how to deal with it. In truth, Saturday night's game wasn't great. You had a true freshman making his first start; he didn't play all that well, and you lost. However, the way Buckeyes fans have responded, there isn't a person in the entire city of Columbus who should still have their job right now. Fire the coaches, fire the players, fire the mayor! Everybody has got to go!  Last Week: 3 | Title Odds: +10006
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            LSU
                    
    
    Trust tree? I'm kind of shocked that LSU was on a bye last week and Lane Kiffin didn't find a way to get his name out there in some kind of stupid news story. It makes me wonder if Kiffin has truly turned a corner now that he's in Baton Rouge. Perhaps he's looking at his team, the environment of the 2026 season, and towards this week's game against Alabama and understands what's possible. Or maybe he's saving it for something really big this week?  Last Week: 6 | Title Odds: +8107
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Ole Miss
                    
    
    I was impressed by what I saw from Ole Miss against Auburn. They were in a bit of a dogfight in the first half, but the Rebels did not let a sluggish start linger into the second half. They scored on every possession they had after halftime except when they were bleeding out the clock to end it in the fourth quarter. It was businesslike, and it's the kind of thing you want to see from a team with a huge game looming.  Last Week: 8 | Title Odds: +18008
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Indiana
                    
    
    I know the Indiana injury report is empty, but you know, golly gee, I just don't believe this team isn't a little dinged up! It certainly seemed like Josh Hoover was hurting before he took that final hit and didn't return to the game in the second half! Seriously, this is a team that really needs the bye this week. They have played nine straight games to open the year without a week off, and you could tell it was taking a toll on them the last few weeks.  Last Week: 7 | Title Odds: +10009
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Texas
                    
    
    Listen, Mississippi State is an awful football team without Kamario Taylor, so there wasn't a whole lot to take away from Texas' 31-3 win over the Bulldogs. That being said, it was nice to see the Longhorns just dominate an opponent from start to finish for once. They hadn't done so since the 30-6 win over UTSA in September. The fans needed a nice, relaxing Saturday and got one.  Last Week: 9 | Title Odds: +105010
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Utah
                    
    
    Kudos to the Utes. They were coming off an important win over Houston, and were in the perfect sandwich spot on the road against Cincinnati with BYU looming this weekend. Plenty of teams would've had a letdown and found themselves in trouble, but not the Utes. It was 42-6 at halftime! Morgan Scalley may be a first-time head coach, but you can't tell by the way this team is prepared every week. I don't know that he's going to win any coach of the year awards, but he deserves to be considered. Last Week: 10 | Title Odds: +300011
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Oregon
                    
    
    I would like to thank Oregon for its 34-26 win over Northwestern. I cannot tell you how much crap I've been taking the last few weeks, keeping Oregon in the top 12 of my power ratings for months now, and I've even mentioned how tempted I was just to ignore the data and punt them out of here to save myself the grief. Then they had that performance against Northwestern and gave us all a glimpse of how good this team can be when it actually plays to its potential. It's crazy how much better the offense looked in its first game with a new playcaller. It turns out that sometimes it really is as simple as "get the ball to your incredibly talented players." Last Week: 11 | Title Odds: +3500012
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Tennessee
                    
    
    The Vols had the week off to recover from their loss to South Carolina and get ready for a massive game against Kentucky this week. Seriously, all offseason college football fans talked about how incredible Week 10 was going to be. Just imagine if, in early August, someone told you that the Week 10 game between Kentucky and Tennessee would be a battle of top-16 teams while only one team in the Ohio State/Oregon game would be ranked. Last Week: 12 | Title Odds: +6400Dropped out: For the first time all season -- nobody

body:
The Bruins shocked the Wildcats in a battle of former Pac-12 rivals as the college basketball season got off to a great start
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:48 am ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College basketball's much-needed return on opening night is Christmas Day … until it starts to get hairy in the second half of a buy game. Just ask North Carolina's Michael Malone, who had to bench his starters midway through the middle of a second-half collapse against Western Carolina. UNC, with help from an untimely technical on the Catamounts, avoided disaster in Monday's 80-72 win, but it was a pucker-worthy showing from a $20 million roster that looks far from the top of the ACC pecking order.The Field of 68 also garners some well-deserved recognition for bringing back the opening day marathon! Grambling State and Northern Illinois played one of Monday's best games in a 4 a.m. banger. The Tigers of Grambling State won 89-87.Let's dive into the rest of the winners and losers from Monday's slate.Winner: Illinois is good at the whole offense thingThe Illini are in the middle of changing their offensive gameplan, pivoting from a team that played slow and relied heavily on pick-and-rolls into a zoom-zoom transition attack that basically has no plays.It took one game to break record books.The 75-point margin of victory was the largest for Illinois at the State Farm Center, which opened in 1963. The Illini fell seven points short of tying the school record for points in a game.  
The Illini drained a program-best 19 3-pointers in a 120-45 romp over FDU. They shot 51 3-pointers. They went 26-for-31 on layups or dunks. 30 of the 46 buckets were assisted. These stat lines were bonkers:Andrej Stojakovic: 20 points, seven rebounds, four assists.Quentin Coleman: 13 points, 10 rebounds, six assists.Ethan Brown: 12 points, nine rebounds, seven assists.Stefan Vaaks: 20 points, four assists, zero turnovers.Seven different players deposited multiple treys. Offensive coordinator Tyler Underwood remains at the top of his craft, and Brad Underwood's willingness to change may be his strongest attribute. Even stronger than excellent evals of guys like Brown, who was a three-star recruit with no high-major offers and all of a sudden looks every bit the part of a multi-year Big Ten starter.Illinois' performance was even more impressive considering the Illini were playing without CBS Sports First Team All-American David Mirkovic, who is recovering from early August foot surgery and underwent an appendectomy Saturday and is out indefinitely.  – Isaac Trotter
Winner: Florida's  Haugh shows why he's a POTY contenderThomas Haugh has two games with four 3-pointers made in his Florida career: In the Elite Eight against Texas Tech in 2025 and on Monday against Miami. Haugh shot a respectable 32.6% on 5.9 attempts from beyond the arc last season, but one of the best shooting nights of his career came in the first game of the new season.And it wasn't just the shooting that stood out. Haugh, known as the ultimate Swiss Army knife, finished with 10 rebounds, four assists and a block and a steal to go along with his 19 points. Michigan State guard Jeremy Fears Jr. was CBS Sports Preseason Player of the Year. However, there is a case for Haugh winning the award. And if this was any indication, it's going to be a special season for Haugh and the Gators. – Cameron Salerno
        
            
                No. 1 Florida opens season with convincing victory vs. Miami: Gators show why they deserve No. 1 ranking
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Loser: Struggles continue for Miami's ReneauReneau led Miami in scoring last year at nearly 18 points per game. It was a big boon to get him back for a fifth year of eligibility, but he had no real answer for Florida's elite frontcourt. Reneau fouled out in 24 minutes and finished with just five points, including an 0-for-5 mark on 2-pointers. Reneau is now shooting just 50% on 2-pointers in his last 25 games against top-50 opponents. Miami will have to get through elite teams if it wants to make the Final Four. It needs more from Reneau to scale that mountain. – Trotter
Winner: All smiles for Cronin, UCLANo. 22 UCLA knocked off No. 5 Arizona 84-75 with a gritty showing up and down the roster. Point guard Trent Perry had 21 points and five assists in a physical win over an old Pac-12 rival. Texas Tech transfer Jaylen Petty is known as a driller, and he did just that with four triples and 13 points. Xavier Booker, much-maligned and stuck in foul trouble, found a way to impact the game in a huge way with a big-time block and triple. Even freshman Nikola Kusturica got in on the fun with nine points, five rebounds, two dimes, three blocks and two steals. The potential No. 1 pick in 2028 is an awesome all-around player. UCLA looks better than its No. 22 ranking. It's too gritty to stink this season. -- TrotterLoser: Iowa State isn't the same ol' Iowa State yetMemphis knocked off No. 18 Iowa State 80-76, behind 26 points from Jayden Reid and an 18-point, eight-rebound showing from SEMO transfer Luke Almodovar. Iowa State entered Monday rated No. 6 on KenPom.com. That seemed high for a roster that lost Milan Momcilovic (to Kentucky) and Joshua Jefferson (to the NBA). The first impression hints that Iowa State isn't close to a top-10 team at the moment. Not without injured defensive maven Killyan Toure. Not if breakout candidate Jamarion Batemon is going to go scoreless. Not if Tamin Lipsey is going to score just 12 points on 13 shots, while looking pretty rusty. T.J. Otzelberger's group has a ton of work to do. – TrotterLoser: Oklahoma suffers historic lossAfter finishing as the first team left out of the 2026 NCAA Tournament field, Oklahoma is already fighting an uphill battle to reach the 2027 Big Dance after the Sooners suffered a stunning 68-64 loss to East Texas A&M. The visiting Lions entered with a 42-87 record in four seasons as a Division I member but did the unthinkable by slaying an SEC foe as a 28.5-point underdog. The Sooners have reached the NCAA Tournament just once under sixth-year coach Porter Moser, and while the event's expansion to 76 teams gives OU a bit more wiggle room, this is already uncomfortable.
This isn't a blue-blood program, but Sooners fans have much higher standards than this program is producing. It's just one game, but this will almost certainly go down as a Quad 4 loss, and it will be a few weeks before OU actually gets a chance to begin undoing the damage against a quality opponent. -- David Cobb
Winner: BYU's offense is a turbo smashNo. 25 BYU's starting lineup makes so much sense. Point guard Rob Wright III can pressure the rim. Collin Chandler is a big-time combo guard who can shoot the 3-pointer and also drive to the cup. Tyler Betsey is a net-shredder. Freshman wing Bruce Branch III can play on or off the ball. Michigan State's 5-in-5 transfer Jaxon Kohler was the skeleton key, though. His ability to play the 5 and stretch the floor keeps the paint open for everything to fall into place. The on-paper vision came to life against Ohio State in the opener. BYU scored 60 (!) points in the second half of Monday's 94-83 win. Wright poured in 33 points, and the rest of that starting lineup cracked double figures. It'd be stunning if BYU doesn't finish as a top-10 offense this year. The personnel is too good. -- Trotter
Winner: Time is now for Zags' FogleGonzaga sophomore wing Davis Fogle is primed for a massive season, and he got busy in Zags' season-opening 78-72 win over Purdue. Fogle totaled 22 points, mixing in slick drives, a sweet catch-and-shoot 3-pointer and 10 attempts from the charity stripe. He was a total handful for this Purdue wing corps that is on the smaller side. -- Trotter
Winner and loser: UCF does UCF stuff while Dior Johnson does Dior Johnson stuffDior Johnson scored 41 points, as Dior Johnson is one to do. Meanwhile, UCF survived FGCU 96-95 in overtime. I don't have high hopes for UCF in the Big 12 this year, but at least Johnson is going to go absolutely insane like once a week. – Trotter
Winner: This is only the beginning for High PointHigh Point coach Flynn Clayman, clad in his ice-cold purple suit, was back in the spotlight, and his Panthers delivered a 72-57 shellacking of a good Liberty squad. High Point's point-of-attack defense is going to be a major strength this season. South Florida transfer CJ Brown and top-150 freshman Trey Pearson are hounding defenders who were draped onto Liberty's point guards for all 40 minutes. 
This High Point squad does not project to be an awesome 3-point shooting team, but its best offense could be this suffocating defense that can lead to numerous good looks in the open floor. Pearson and ex-Arizona walk-on Conrad Martinez combined for 21 points, seven rebounds, three assists and just one turnover. Oh, and they both were coming off the bench. Clayman's got another real-deal squad. High Point is currently favored by double figures in every single Big South game. – TrotterWinner: This is only the beginning for Murray State, tooMurray State has some of the deepest pockets at the mid-major ranks, and this roster looks like a high-major outfit. Full stop. The Racers buried Tennessee State 94-64, with a new defensive recipe. Murray State has flipped from a passive to an aggressive defensive scheme, and it passed the first test with flying colors. Tennessee State, filled with numerous former high-major names like Arterio Morris (Texas), Aaron Bradshaw (Kentucky) and Ty-Laur Johnson (Wake Forest), turned the basketball over a whopping 26 times. Murray State was everywhere. Sophomore wing Roman Domon was awesome, finishing with 22 points, five rebounds, two assists, a block and a steal. Domon has a chance to get paid to play basketball for a very long time. This team is deep and talented, but it also has so much room to grow. If the first impression is any indication, Murray State has the pieces to earn an at-large bid. That hasn't happened for the Missouri Valley since 2021. – Trotter

        LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers couldn't have asked for a better start to the 2026-27 season. Their grand experiment adding James and Jaylen Brown to create a star-studded starting lineup with Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid has gotten off to a fantastic start. The 76ers are 7-1 after a 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls on Monday night. The vibes in Philly are, as they say, immaculate, and it's allowed James to have a little fun added to his 24th season in the league. During the third quarter of the Sixers win over Chicago, James tried to chase down an outlet pass and went charging into the stands, bumping into a fan who had a cup of wine in the Philly crowd.LeBron, who is the NBA's preeminent Wine Guy, decided he'd take a quick sip to see what the fan was working with before jogging back to the court. 
After the game, LeBron was asked about the moment and offered a quick review of the wine selection available at Xfinity Mobile Arena. 
"I spilled some of his wine, so I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm, how good it was," James said, via The Athletic. "It was aight. It was aight."
James finished the game with 15 points, nine assists and seven rebounds in 31 minutes, doing a bit of everything in his supporting role for a Sixers team that continues to roll. Maxey led the way with 26 points and 11 assists, while Jaylen Brown added 25 points and 11 rebounds and VJ Edgecombe made it three starters over 20 points with a 21-point outing. 
The scary thing about the Sixers is it hasn't felt like they've come close to hitting their full stride in terms of complete performances, but they overwhelm teams with their talent and have had a knack for pulling away late. As long as they keep that up, fans will be happy to share a bit of their vino with James as a treat.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto currently holds the record with a $325 million contract, while two are tied with a $43.33M AAV

        Tarik Skubal is about to become a very, very rich man. The two-time Cy Young winner and arguably the best pitcher in baseball hits free agency this winter, and it stands to reason that he'll break the record for highest-paid pitcher in MLB history, both by total value and average annual value.By total value, Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto currently holds that record thanks to the 12-year, $325 million contract he signed ahead of the 2024 season (we're eliminating Shohei Ohtani from the running for obvious reasons, though his 10-year, $700 million deal would clearly lead the list). PitcherYearsTotal valueYoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers12$325 millionGerrit Cole, Yankees9$324 millionStephen Strasburg, Nationals9$245 millionJacob deGrom, Rangers5$185 millionAaron Nola, Phillies7$172 millionCarlos Rodón, Yankees6$162 millionAs for AAV, Ohtani again tops the class at $70 million a year, but for those who only pitch, Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander share the record at $43.33 million annually.The expectation is that Skubal will break both records, even as the owners try to tamp down on spending in the ongoing CBA negotiations. Just how high could those figures go? CBS Sports experts pulled out their calculators.
Contract predictionsMike Axisa: Seven years and $325.5 million. That's $46.5 million per season and it would break the records for average annual value (Max Scherzer's and Justin Verlander's $43.3 million) and total guarantee (Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million) for a pitcher. I would expect there to be an opt out because those are just the cost of doing business these days. Maybe even multiple opt outs. Scott Boras loves to break records, though, and this contract allows him to break two.Dayn Perry: I'll say eight years, $350 million. Likewise, that sets the record for total contract value and AAV for a pitcher. Normally, I'd ding him a bit for those elbow problems in his walk year, but he was mostly dominant after returning ahead of schedule. I also think Skubal will benefit from an aggressive pre-lockout market and from a pretty thin free agent class overall.
Matt Snyder: Eight years, $400 million. This gets him the record deal for pitchers both in terms of the guarantee and the average annual value. I'm probably going too low on the years, but I feel like teams have been burned so many times before on the length of pitcher deals due to injury that this holds down the market a bit. Ever so slightly. I do think there will be opt outs after years three and five.

title: Watching Marcis 'Baby Shaq' Ponder's debut: Why Florida State's massive freshman center is must-see TV - CBS Sports
description: The 7-foot, 285-pound freshman center could be one of the breakout stars of the 2026-27 season
body:
The 7-foot, 285-pound freshman center could be one of the breakout stars of the 2026-27 season

        TAMPA, Fla. -- Less than 16 minutes into Marcis Ponder's college career, fans inside Benchmark International Arena were chanting his name ... kinda.After Florida State's 7-foot, 285-pound freshman center hustled in an attempt to secure an offensive rebound, he was fouled. That meant another trip to the free-throw line and a chance to add stats to his already impressive night. Once he stepped onto the line, fans started chanting "Baby Shaq," a nickname Ponder earned when he was just a teenager.There are some similarities in playstyle between Ponder and Shaquille O'Neal's games, which makes his nickname — and the fans chanting it — even more fitting. O'Neal, who became one of the most dominant players of his era for his blend of size, strength and athleticism, inspired a generation of players to live and dominate the game from inside the paint.That's Ponder's game to a T. He is a down-low physical finisher who operates almost solely in the paint. He sets hard screens and gobbles up rebounds on both ends of the floor. Ponder, who played football growing up, looks impossible to move, so imagine being on the opposing end of a screen or having to fight around him for a rebound.
Doesn't sound fun.
Ponder's interior dominance on the offensive glassIt didn't take long for Ponder to announce himself to the college basketball universe during Florida State's 113-69 win on Monday against Florida A&M and show why he might be one of the most entertaining and physically imposing players in the sport. After winning the opening tip, Ponder hustled to secure an offensive rebound off a missed shot and used his frame to finish inside the restricted area with ease. It was a sign of things to come.Less than 40 seconds after scoring his first official points as a college player, Ponder was back for more. After a missed 3-pointer at the top of the key, Ponder was all alone in the paint where he grabbed the offensive rebound and simultaneously threw down a two-handed dunk. 
And just like that, less than a minute and a half into the game, Ponder had four points and two rebounds (both offensive).Ponder, the No. 43-ranked player in the 2026 class by 247Sports, was a huge recruiting win for FSU second-year coach Luke Loucks. He committed to Florida State last summer over Cincinnati, Illinois, Indiana, Miami, Providence and Texas less than a few months after Loucks took the job at his alma mater after a stint as an assistant coach for the Sacramento Kings.
        
            
                No. 1 Florida opens season with convincing victory vs. Miami: Gators show why they deserve No. 1 ranking
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Based on early returns, Ponder will be a key building block for Loucks and Florida State as the program looks to return to the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2021. 
Just two and a half minutes into the game, Ponder gets a break on the FSU sideline where he stands near the end of the bench, waiting to get back in the game. He doesn't have to wait long. After just over four minutes, Ponder checks back in and doesn't take long for him to get involved. Florida A&M opts for a 2-3 zone defense, which clears the lane for Ponder to find open space and crash the boards for another offensive rebound while drawing contact. He proceeds to step to the free-throw line and miss a pair, his only misses from the charity stripe in the first half.And just like that, Ponder has 11 points and seven rebounds in just 10 minutes of play in the first half. It was on the free-throw line where Ponder got the "Baby Shaq" chants while knocking down both attempts right before Florida State went to the locker room with a 27-point advantage.
Ponder finishes with a 15-point and 11-rebound double-double in his debutLess than two minutes into the second half, Ponder is right back to work on the offensive glass. The behemoth of a freshman secured a missed shot around the rim and put it back up for an easy bucket. While running back on defense, Ponder appears to voice his displeasure that no foul was called on the play.  It results in a technical foul that garners boos from the fans still lingering inside the arena.Moments later, Ponder checks out of the game after picking up his third foul. He's two rebounds shy of a double-double, something he achieved in an exhibition game against Auburn last month with 13 points and 21 rebounds in a win over the Tigers. Sure, it was in a game that didn't count, but it piqued the interest of the college basketball world as a sign of things to come for the FSU rookie.
On Monday night in his official college debut, Ponder finished with 15 points, 11 rebounds and a block.Florida A&M, ranked No. 323 on KenPom.com, isn't exactly a season-defining test for Florida State, but the schedule will get tougher very fast. Florida State has a date in one week vs. No. 1 Florida on Nov. 10. It will be the biggest game for Loucks and Florida State since he took over at his alma mater. Not only are the Gators the top-ranked team in the country, but they also have the best and most experienced frontcourt in college basketball, featuring the trio of Alex Condon, Thomas Haugh and Rueben Chinyelu. It will be a massive test for the massive Ponder and his Seminoles. 
Ponder is already must-watch TV. And Florida State might have college basketball's next star center.

title: Mock trades for Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr.: Why Chiefs, Raiders could stand out as top fits - CBS Sports
description: Thomas has struggled after an outstanding rookie year
body:
Thomas has struggled after an outstanding rookie year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:50 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Amid a difficult 2024 season, then-rookie wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. was a major silver lining for the Jacksonville Jaguars. The first-round selection had 87 receptions for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns in his debut campaign, earned a Pro Bowl honor and finished fourth in a loaded Offensive Rookie of the Year race.Now, the situation has done a complete 180. The Jaguars are 5-2 and one of the best teams in the NFL, but Thomas is merely a fringe contributor. His 10 catches this year rank fifth on the team, and his 117 yards are tied for fifth. He has played 44% of the team's offensive snaps, the third-highest among wide receivers, but a figure that has fluctuated week to week. He played just 21% of the snaps in a narrow Week 6 loss to the Texans before playing 52% of the snaps (and catching a touchdown pass) in a blowout win over the Colts. That touchdown snag was his first catch since Week 4.Coach Liam Coen and quarterback Trevor Lawrence backed Thomas and highlighted his importance on several occasions."I was super excited," Lawrence said of the touchdown pass Sunday. "It's a team game, and you want to see all your teammates have success, especially the situation with BT. I mean, the guy's so talented, he's a great player, and obviously hasn't been the easiest for him lately, but he's been working extremely hard to make plays."
The Jaguars have a deep stead of receiving options: Wide receivers Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, tight end Brenton Strange and running back Bhayshul Tuten all have more catches than Thomas does. But Thomas also adds a deep downfield element that no one else on the team does, even if it hasn't resulted in many box score contributions.If the Jaguars are willing to part ways with Thomas — and that's a major "if" — there would be plenty of suitors. Here are four who could make sense, along with the packages they could offer. In this instance, we'll use the trade package for another 2024 first-round wide receiver who's had many ups and downs, Marvin Harrison Jr., as a framework. The Texans sent 2027 second- and seventh-round picks to the Cardinals for Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kansas City ChiefsChiefs receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr.Jaguars receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 sixth-round pickThe Chiefs have an extra third-round pick in 2027 from the Trent McDuffie trade and a desperate need for a wide receiver who can stretch the defense. Patrick Mahomes has not completed a pass 20+ yards downfield in any of his last three games. In Sunday's crucial loss to the Broncos, the Chiefs' leading receiver was running back Emmett Johnson, followed by tight end Travis Kelce. Rashee Rice, the team's leading wide receiver, is mostly a quick-game target whose production comes after the catch.The big question with this trade is why Jacksonville would want to help out a fellow AFC contender. It's much easier to simply keep Thomas Jr.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Pittsburgh Steelers
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Steelers receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr.Jaguars receive: 2027 third-round pick, T Dylan CookAgain, the big question here is "Why would the Jaguars help out another team with playoff aspirations?" That's why this offer is bigger than the two that follow, from either non-AFC or non-contending teams.The Steelers, who have been hit hard by injuries, could try to sweeten the deal by adding Cook, a backup tackle. The Jaguars recently lost Anton Harrison for the season, stretching their tackle depth very thin. Cook lost his starting spot to Max Iheanachor, but he has been a capable starter before.
Las Vegas RaidersRaiders receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr.Jaguars receive: 2027 third-round pickThe Raiders, unlike the Chiefs and Steelers, are not expected to contend this season. Even though they're 4-4, they're 1-4 over their past five games and have a tough schedule upcoming. Furthermore, the Raiders have a clear and obvious need at wide receiver, both currently and in the future when No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza takes over for Kirk Cousins. Brock Bowers is a star, but finding a complement is critical. Thomas could be the answer if he rediscovers his rookie-year form, or he could just be part of the answer. Regardless, making a run at Thomas would be within reason.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Washington CommandersCommanders receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr.Jaguars receive: 2027 fourth-round pick, DT Shy TuttleThe Commanders are a team that could go one way or the other ahead of the trade deadline. They're only 2-4-1, but they play in the woeful NFC East. Week 9 will be crucial; if the Commanders can spring an upset of the Rams, they could shift toward buying. If they lose and the Giants and/or Cowboys win, selling could make more sense (though coach Dan Quinn and GM Adam Peters will be keen on keeping their jobs, meaning they might not want to sell).
Thomas was a college teammate of Jayden Daniels at LSU. The Commanders would look at this as an investment for the present but also for the future. Terry McLaurin is out for the season, and there's a potential out in his contract this offseason. Stefon Diggs is on a one-year deal. Throwing in Tuttle could help push this deal over the edge, as Jacksonville is looking for interior defensive line help after DaVon Hamilton's injury.

title: Trey Kaufman-Renn makes Kansas debut: Ex-Purdue star finally takes floor for Jayhawks - CBS Sports

body:
Kaufman-Renn came off the bench to score nine points in the Jayhawks' 95-65 win vs. Fordham

                    at
    11:56 pm ET

        Trey Kaufman-Renn made his highly anticipated debut with No. 17 Kansas on Monday during its 95-65 win over Fordham. The former Purdue star forward, who is currently eligible to play during the 2026-27 season after being granted a motion for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA, finished with nine points, five rebounds and a block.Kaufman-Renn didn't start in the first half for Kansas, but was in the lineup at the start of the second half and logged 23 minutes for the Jayhawks. "You guys will think I'm full of it, which I'm sure that many of you actually do totally 100% believe, but the guy came here totally cold," Kansas coach Bill Self said. "He was in bad shape and all that stuff. So I did want to evaluate him here on that. And in the meantime, we did check some boxes, just as we would with any transfer. But it is a difference. You guys could tell he's kind of a connector. Everybody's just going to be better with him on the floor."  Kaufman-Renn did not play in Kansas' exhibition game against Duke days after being cleared to play.
The former Purdue star played five seasons with the program before joining the Jayhawks. However, since he redshirted his first year, he has only played four years of college basketball despite being a Class of 2021 high school recruit. Kaufman-Renn was granted an unprecedented sixth year of eligibility, which differs from the traditional five-for-five cases players are currently suing for in court. After signing with Purdue out of high school, Kaufman-Renn didn't suit up during the 2021-22 season after suffering a knee injury in early November 2021 that required surgery. After redshirting during his freshman season, Kaufman-Renn played four subsequent years and developed into one of the best power forwards in the sport.Kansas was already over the 15-man roster limit after adding back Tre White and Melvin Council Jr. — two players who played last season for the Jayhawks and are seeking a fifth year of eligibility — but was able to add the former Purdue star after freshman guard Grant Mordini suffered a season-ending patellar tendon injury.
Why TKR's case is different from othersKaufman-Renn is one scholastic year older than athletes fighting in court for an additional season. Under the NCAA's new age-based eligibility model, Kaufman-Renn's college eligibility would've run out because he technically was on a roster for five seasons, despite playing in just four of those years. The difference with Kaufman-Renn is that the first of his five college seasons was spent redshirting. He didn't play his freshman year. Although he started his college career in a different year (2021), he still only played four seasons of college basketball.What is complicated about Kaufman-Renn's case is that he was drafted No. 59 overall by the Minnesota Timberwolves this past summer. However, seniors who have exhausted their eligibility are automatically eligible for the NBA Draft. They don't technically have to "declare" for the draft, which is part of the distinction that high-major conferences are fighting over right now. 
If a player declares for the draft — as former St. John's star RJ Luis Jr. did — he can't return to play college sports.Kaufman-Renn averaged 14.2 points, 8.3 rebounds, and 2.5 assists during the 2025-26 season at Purdue and would've likely been a preseason All-American if he were guaranteed to be eligible this season. With Kaufman-Renn, White and Council, the Jayhawks have a roster capable of competing at the top of the Big 12.

title: Could Tyson Bagent save Ravens' playoff hopes? Lamar Jackson injury raises a costly trade question - CBS Sports
description: The Ravens are 4-4, Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve after undergoing thumb surgery on his throwing hand, and suddenly Baltimo
body:
The Ravens are 4-4, Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve after undergoing thumb surgery on his throwing hand, and suddenly Baltimore has a much bigger problem than anyone could have imagined even just a few days ago. Jackson had already missed three games with a high-ankle sprain before returning Sunday against Buffalo, only to injure his thumb on his first play back. Backup Tyler Huntley also left that game with a toe injury; undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was pressed into action and looked like, well, an undrafted rookie who had taken exactly zero reps with the first team. And with the NFL trade deadline approaching, Baltimore has to decide whether to stick with its current QB room or find help elsewhere.The Ravens could look to trade for an experienced quarterback. But there's another option worth considering: a younger, largely unproven backup whose upside -- and familiarity with Baltimore's offense -- could make him an appealing target. And that brings us to Bears backup Tyson Bagent.According to Pro Football Talk, Baltimore could explore trading for Bagent, although acquiring him "won't be cheap." How expensive? Chicago Tribune reporter Brad Biggs suggested back in February that it could take a second-round pick, or equivalent compensation, to convince the Bears to make a deal. That wasn't a reported asking price, but it tells you something about how Chicago values its backup quarterback.
And if you're Baltimore, that's where things get complicated. Because while Bagent might give the Ravens their best chance to remain competitive until Jackson returns -- assuming he returns this season -- we're still talking about a former undrafted free agent with six career starts, three touchdown passes and nine interceptions.So how much is that worth? And what does history tell us about teams trading valuable draft picks for largely unproven quarterbacks?The answers are … interesting.Why Bagent makes sense for BaltimoreThere's an obvious reason Bagent's name has surfaced in connection with the Ravens, and it goes beyond their suddenly depleted quarterback room. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle spent last season in Chicago in the same role, where he worked directly with Bagent.
And Doyle wasn't shy about how he felt about the quarterback."Tyson is no-nonsense," Doyle said during training camp in 2025. "He's businesslike. Football's really important to him."That familiarity matters. Doyle knows what Bagent does well, where he struggles and, perhaps most importantly, what he can reasonably be asked to do. And because Doyle helped implement Ben Johnson's offense in Chicago before bringing elements of that system to Baltimore -- including pre-snap motion, play-action and formation versatility -- Bagent would arrive with some familiarity with the concepts and expectations.That doesn't mean Bagent will suddenly play like Jackson. And the Ravens wouldn't ask him to. They need somebody who can execute what's being asked, protect the football and give Baltimore a chance to win while Jackson recovers.
But what should the Ravens be willing to give up for that?What history says about trading for unproven quarterbacksWe went back through quarterback trades dating to 2007, focusing on players who had started 10 or fewer NFL games before another team acquired them. We looked at their performance before the trade, what their new teams gave up and, most importantly, what happened after they arrived.And there have been some clear successes, starting with Matt Schaub.Houston sent Atlanta two second-round picks and swapped first-round selections in 2007 for Schaub, who had started just twice in three seasons with the Falcons. He became Houston's starter for seven seasons, throwing for more than 23,000 yards and helping the Texans reach the playoffs twice.A decade later, San Francisco sent New England a second-rounder for Jimmy Garoppolo, who also had just two NFL starts. The trade came at the 2017 deadline, and Garoppolo went 5-0 after taking over as the starter for a 1-10 team that finished 6-10. He eventually went 38-17 as the 49ers' starter and helped them reach the Super Bowl.
Schaub and Garoppolo, it turns out, are the exceptions.Indianapolis traded former first-round receiver Phillip Dorsett to New England for Jacoby Brissett in 2017. Brissett started 30 games for the Colts, with 31 touchdowns and 13 interceptions. Dallas, meanwhile, gave up a fourth-rounder for Trey Lance in 2023 to serve as Dak Prescott's backup. The former No. 3 overall pick started just once for the Cowboys before leaving in free agency.Then there's Joshua Dobbs, who was traded three times. Jacksonville gave up a fifth-rounder for him in 2019 and never started him. Arizona traded for him in 2023, got eight starts and a 1-7 record, then sent him to Minnesota, where he briefly became one of the NFL's best stories before eventually losing his starting job.The most encouraging recent example? Malik Willis.Originally a 2022 third-round pick, Tennessee traded Willis to Green Bay for a seventh-rounder in 2024 after he'd struggled through three starts with the Titans. All Willis did for the Packers was go 2-1 in three starts, throwing six touchdowns without an interception during his time there.
Of the 10 trades we looked at, only five resulted in the quarterback starting at least eight games for his new team. Just three -- Schaub, Garoppolo and Brissett -- made 16 or more starts.It's not an exhaustive list, but the larger point is hard to miss. Teams routinely trade for quarterbacks they believe can offer more than they've shown. Occasionally, they find a long-term starter. More often, they're giving up future draft picks for somebody who never becomes the answer.Why the right fit can change everythingOf course, evaluating quarterbacks isn't as simple as comparing stat lines, particularly when they've barely played.
Schaub found success playing for Gary Kubiak in Houston, while Garoppolo benefited from Kyle Shanahan's offense in San Francisco. And Willis looked like a completely different quarterback when Matt LaFleur built Green Bay's game plans around what he did best.Matt Cassel offers another example. The former seventh-rounder played well in place of an injured Tom Brady in New England in 2008, then struggled during his first season in Kansas City. But when former Patriots offensive coordinator Charlie Weis arrived in 2010, Cassel threw 27 touchdowns against seven interceptions, made the Pro Bowl and helped the Chiefs win the AFC West. He never sustained that level of success after Weis left.None of this happens in a vacuum. Coaching, scheme and supporting cast all matter and what a quarterback accomplished in one offense doesn't necessarily tell us what he'll do in another.
Which brings us back to Doyle and Bagent.Can the Ravens actually survive without Lamar?We looked at this question earlier in the season when Seattle lost Sam Darnold, and the findings were revealing.From 2015-2025, 41 teams were above .500 after losing their starting quarterback. Their backups went just 55-82, yet 24 of those teams still made the playoffs. Twelve won at least one postseason game, and four eventually won the Super Bowl.So, yes, good teams can survive losing their starter. But there's a catch, and it's a big one.
Among those teams, 67.9% made the playoffs when the backup needed to start just one to three games. That fell to 38.5% when the replacement started at least four games, and just 16.7% when the absence stretched to seven or more starts.Baltimore currently isn't above .500, but the point remains: Asking a backup to keep a talented team competitive for two or three weeks is one thing. Asking him to do it for two months -- or potentially the remainder of the season -- is something else entirely. Especially when the quarterback you're asking to do all this may not be on the roster right now.And that's what makes Jackson's uncertain recovery timeline so important. The Ravens aren't necessarily looking for somebody to replace their franchise QB. They're looking for somebody who can keep the season from getting away from them before he returns.
So what's Bagent actually worth?Based on history alone, a fourth-round pick might seem reasonable for Bagent, given that he's played so little in his career. But there's no reason for Chicago to accept such an offer when it values Bagent as Caleb Williams' backup and has him under contract through 2027.Which means Baltimore may have to look elsewhere. One possibility is recently-benched-and-demoted-to-QB3 Jacoby Brissett, currently of the Arizona Cardinals, but for how long is up in the air. The Cards haven't indicated they're shopping him, but his experience – and his current place on the depth chart – could make him a consideration before the trade deadline.Yes, Schaub and Garoppolo proved that teams can find legitimate starters on somebody else's bench. Both were Day 2 picks, however, while Bagent went undrafted out of Division II Shepherd University. But there are plenty of examples of teams paying for potential and getting little in return. And Baltimore's immediate need for a quarterback doesn't automatically make Bagent more valuable.Doyle knows Bagent better than most coaches around the league, and that familiarity could give the Ravens a better chance of making this work. History says a capable backup in the right situation can keep a season alive, particularly if the starter's absence is relatively short. And, by the way, Baltimore just signed Austin Reed to its practice squad -- another quarterback who worked with Doyle in Chicago last year.But if Chicago really wants something approaching a second-round pick, Baltimore has to decide whether it's paying for a quarterback who can help save the season -- or simply paying a premium because it's running out of options.

schema.headline: Could Tyson Bagent save Ravens' playoff hopes? Lamar Jackson injury raises a costly trade question - CBS Sports

        Draymond Green made it to November (barely) before earning his first ejection of the 2026-27 NBA season. On Monday night, Green took exception to getting knocked over by Phoenix Suns center Khaman Maluach posting up in transition and got up and tackled Maluach, wrapping him up with both arms and throwing him to the ground -- Maluach still made a basket for an and-1. Dillon Brooks then ran over to confront Green, which unsurprisingly led to a brief scuffle between the two and Green was eventually given two technical fouls and ejected in an eventual Warriors win.
"I was just trying to de-escalate it," Brooks said. "He was just tweaking all game."The ejection is Green's 31st of his career and he now has three technical fouls this season, tied for the most in the league. Once a player reaches 16 technicals in a season, it triggers an automatic one-game suspension. 
Without Green, the Warriors surged back from a double-digit second-half deficit to get a 116-113 win thanks to Stephen Curry's heroics with 34 points and a huge game off the bench from Charles Bassey, who scored 19 points and pulled down eight rebounds in 22 minutes due to Green's absence. Bassey's 19 points in 22 minutes off the bench on Monday night equals Green's 19 points in 159 minutes of play this season. Green does lead the Warriors in assists (6.3 per game), and the offense hums around him with Curry and rookie star Yaxel Lendeborg combining for more than 50 points per game. 
With the win, Golden State improved to 5-3 on the season and now sits in seventh in the Western Conference standings early in the season as the Warriors try to claw their way back to the playoffs for the first time in three seasons.

title: Six lessons from Week 8: Bears emerge as top-tier Super Bowl contenders, Chiefs must address glaring flaws - CBS Sports

body:
The NFL is always full of surprises -- season to season, week to week and, on Sundays, hour to hour.The Week 8 schedule was absolutely loaded, but the two best games of the Sunday slate ended up being Bengals-Titans and Cowboys-Cardinals. If you had Gardner Minshew coming off the bench and throwing three touchdowns to lead a double-digit comeback and Joe Burrow accounting for six touchdowns -- and throwing three interceptions -- go buy a lottery ticket.And that was only the early window. Later in the day, Bo Nix went from zero to hero again, leading a stunning double-digit comeback against the Chiefs. Overall, there were five double-digit comeback wins, the most of any week this season.So yes, it may be November, but we're still learning, still being surprised, still finding out what's real and what's not. And the Bears capped a wild weekend by showing they are very much for real.
1. The Bears are top-tier Super Bowl contendersIf you had high expectations for Jeffery Simmons in Chicago -- and I very much did -- they somehow still weren't high enough, at least for one game. The Bears' 34-17 dismantling of the reigning-champion Seahawks was a fever dream for any Chicago fan.Simmons delivered six tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss and a pass broken up in his team debut, but that outstanding stat line still doesn't come close to telling the full story.The Bears allowed 3.0 yards per play with Simmons on the field. They came in allowing 6.3 yards per play, worst in the NFL.That included 2.6(!) net yards per pass attempt allowed. For reference, the best net yards per attempt defense this year is the Steelers at ... 6.1.Bears pass rushers not named Simmons terrorized Sam Darnold all night, too. Montez Sweat in particular had his best game in recent memory.This is what superstars do. They wreck plays, and when they don't, they allow others to. Sam Darnold was running for his life all night en route to just 188 passing yards on 5.0 net yards per attempt. I found it fitting that the Seahawks acquired Quenton Nelson this week, and yet Simmons stole the show. And that's no shade to Nelson. Simmons is that good.
Caleb Williams, meanwhile, was superb. The stats didn't pop, but what makes him so good is that he can have absurd statistical games and he can have just really efficient, high-floor games. Against one of the league's best defenses, Williams had no turnovers and took just one sack. His 7.3 yards per attempt were the best by any player against Seattle this season.Stars make the world go 'round. They give you a chance. But supporting casts lift you from "having a chance" to "being a force," and the Bears have an awesome supporting cast. Ben Johnson is a top-five coach. Luther Burden III is an ultra-fun wide receiver who eats up one-on-one coverage and has tons of juice after the catch. Outside of his fumble, Colston Loveland was excellent. Rome Odunze is the big, physical guy who wins intermediate/deep throws in the middle of the field, a crucial area to attack. He has been terrific recently. The offensive line is outstanding. Everything has fallen into place.There are still weaknesses. The cornerbacks are a concern. But the NFL is about figuring out ways to either hide, overcome or fix those weaknesses. Star power is the best way to do it, and the Bears have superstars at quarterback and, now, on defense.
The Seahawks hadn't lost a game by five or more points in nearly two years. They lost this one by 17. The Bears were probably a second-tier Super Bowl contender this time one week ago. After Monday night? Welcome to the top tier, Chicago.2. Don't count out the Lions, though*whispers* Here come the Lions.It seems like all the discourse from the Lions' gritty 19-15 win over the Vikings was about how bad Kyler Murray has been. Maybe -- just maybe -- we should focus on Detroit.The offense is currently third in EPA per play and success rate and sixth in explosive play rate. Jared Goff has thrown for 15 touchdowns and one interception and is playing like a legit MVP candidate. He won't win the award, but he should garner votes. His ability to manage pressure -- long his biggest weakness -- has been at career-best levels this year. Jameson Williams looks like a stud again, and we already know Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown are awesome. Detroit ranks third in run blocking and fourth in pass blocking in PFF's metrics.
The defense, meanwhile, is eighth in success rate and 13th in EPA per play over the past two weeks. Brian Branch's return has been huge. Kerby Joseph could be back soon. The secondary has been miles better since the bye. Up front, Aidan Hutchinson remains a star, and Alim McNeil and Tyleik Williams are playing well inside.This could be the NFC version of the Bengals: elite offense plus just enough defensive playmaking to be a threat.3. The Chiefs have multiple issues to fix, and the trade deadline must be the time to fix themIn a vacuum, the Chiefs' loss to the Broncos was just that: one loss. Yes, it was a disappointing one, given the chance to put a vice grip on the division, but it's just one loss.
In the big picture, this game revealed multiple significant issues -- issues that will cost the Chiefs when a loss isn't just a game lost, but a season lost.These are the three things I'm quite worried about:Andy Reid's continued game mismanagementShort-yardage issuesAbsolutely no downfield presenceIn the fourth quarter alone, Reid punted on a fourth-and-inches and, up three, had Harrison Butker (who was 2-for-6 from 50+ entering the game) attempt a 54-yard field goal in the rain. Butker missed. Both of those decisions were key moments of the Chiefs blowing an 11-point lead in the final quarter.Reid has one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time, yet made two incredibly conservative decisions. This is far from the first time. The field goal decision was particularly infuriating because being up six isn't that much more helpful than being up three, and Mahomes is, historically, better on fourth and 8 to fourth and 12 than Butker is from 50+ this year. You can read more of my thoughts on Reid blowing it here.
The short-yardage issues aren't new, either, and they play into Reid's mismanagement. Mahomes has not attempted a quarterback sneak since 2019. If that's how it is, fine. But the Chiefs still have to find another way to consistently get one yard. Kansas City only gains a first down on 62.5% of its plays when it has 1 yard or less to go, 23rd in the league this year. This loomed very large, of course, at the end on Sunday, when Kansas City failed to convert on multiple goal-to-go opportunities at the 1-yard line.The Chiefs' wide receiving corps is hurting in both the short yardage and the (lack of) big yardage. For the latter, there is no deep threat. Mahomes has gone three straight games without completing a pass 20+ yards downfield. The pass-catching options are, frankly, appalling for a Super Bowl contender. Rashee Rice is a YAC guy. Xavier Worthy just doesn't provide a lot. Even Travis Kelce had two bad drops. And in the short yardage, wouldn't it be nice to have a guy who can win a 50/50 ball? A big catch radius? A guy who wins one-on-one?George Pickens is the dream add here, but Kansas City must do something. Must. Mahomes is too good. Kenneth Walker III is too good. You just can't pass up many opportunities when you have Mahomes. The Chiefs have extra draft capital. Look at other Super Bowl contenders making big trades this season. If you're not giving Mahomes the best chance possible (within reason) to win a Super Bowl every year, you're being wasteful. It's already bad that the pass-catcher is such a huge issue for a second straight year, but the Chiefs have a chance to change that.
4. Adonai Mitchell rocksA week ago, I floated Adonai Mitchell as a potential solution for the Chiefs' wide receiver woes. He was coming off a zero-catch game, and Omar Cooper Jr. was emerging for the Jets.Now? I think Mitchell might be a legit part of the Jets' long-term build. Sunday, he had seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown. But it's more than the stats. It's how he looked as he accrued them.
That is legitimate star-level film. I know the Raiders' cornerbacks are young and not great, but Mitchell looked like varsity against JV.
Mitchell was a throw-in in the Sauce Gardner trade. An afterthought. His career was synonymous with a 75-yard catch in which he toasted multiple defenders, only to fumble the ball 1 yard before entering the end zone uncontested. The talent has always been there.He was off to a strong start this season before a freak finger injury suffered in practice. If he has finally put it all together, the Gardner trade -- already a landslide win for New York -- got even more lopsided.5. Gregory Rousseau belongs in the Defensive Player of the Year conversation.In all likelihood, you only heard the name Gregory Rousseau in connection to the Lamar Jackson injury. With Jackson and, later, Tyler Huntley out, the Bills crushed the Ravens 36-10, turning a highly anticipated game into a snoozefest.
But if that's all you heard, you missed out on Rousseau being an absolute menace. He only played 30 snaps because of the blowout, but he still managed seven pressures and a sack. Watch him toss Roger Rosengarten aside on the sack.
Shortly thereafter, he destroyed a drive on his own.
Here's where Rousseau stands through eight weeks:46 pressures (most in NFL)22 quarterback hits (tied for most)20.4% pressure rate (third)7 sacks (tied for third)3 forced fumbles (tied for third)He has crucial splash plays -- a strip sack to seal a win over the Texans in Week 1, another strip sack in Week 2 -- and impressive consistency, with at least six pressures in six of Buffalo's seven games.Will Anderson Jr. is rightfully a comfortable favorite (+250, per DraftKings) to win Defensive Player of the Year. But Rousseau has quietly climbed up to +1200, the fifth-shortest odds. He absolutely belongs in the conversation and has plenty of time to become a bigger part of it.6. The alternate uniforms stinkI can't believe I am "Old man yells at cloud"-ing this, but the Lions' and the Jaguars' uniforms were truly unsightly. Let's start with the Lions, whose uniforms looked like the Panthers had washed their white laundry and their dark laundry together.
Jahmyr Gibbs looks cool because he can make anything look cool. That's what happens when you are cool. But these are bad.The same thing goes for the Jaguars. A few days later, I feel a little bit better about Jacksonville's getup, but I don't love it.
The helmets being such a departure from the rest of the uniform my biggest complaint. It kind of felt like someone putting together a sensible shirt and pants combo and then throwing on a clashing hat, just because.The NFL wants alternate jerseys, but some things are better left untouched. Fear not, though, Lions and Jaguars fans. You're still not nearly as bad as the Bills' "Nickel City" eyesore from Week 3. This looked straight out of an unlicensed video game.
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            We can do better than this, right?

title: Ranking NFL's best new coordinators: Packers, Steelers assistants lead top 10 at midseason - CBS Sports
