body:
These 10 coordinators inherited difficult circumstances, adapted to significant injuries and delivered immediate results in their new homes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:54 am ET
                        
                •
            
            10 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The path from star coordinator to elite head coach is as clear as ever. Look no further than defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald, Kyle Shanahan, Sean McVay, or, more recently, Ben Johnson and Liam Coen. Finding the next one of those guys could change the fortune of any franchise, and those types of coaches can be found occupying offensive and defensive coordinator roles today. So which new coordinators are making the biggest, positive impact in their NFL homes through the first half or so of the 2026 season? Here is a look at the top 10 plus a few honorable mentions. Honorable mentions: New York Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich, Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, Buffalo Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator Declan DoyleThe Baltimore Ravens were the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (29.0) through the first four weeks of the 2026 season under new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle when Lamar Jackson was healthy. Without Jackson since Week 5, Baltimore averages just 15.8 points per game, the fifth-lowest in the league. After Doyle surprised the Atlanta Falcons with backup Tyler Huntley in a 30-23 overtime road win, the Ravens have lost three in a row.
If Jackson can shake off his injury woes, Doyle could easily get the Ravens offense back on track. That sadly appears to be a big if at the moment. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury  The Seattle Seahawks experienced a tough offseason of attrition, losing offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak to the Las Vegas Raiders and Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker to the Chiefs. New offensive coordinator Brian Fleury also got hit with an injury to quarterback Sam Darnold on the first drive of the season, and Darnold has been a rollercoaster the rest of the way: His -0.67 expected points added (EPA) per dropback when pressured is the worst in the NFL this season. Perhaps the addition of Quenton Nelson can help calm Darnold down on that front while he aims to find his footing post-glute injury. Both of Seattle's top running backs, Zach Charbonnet (torn ACL) and first-round rookie Jadarian Price (chest), had yet to be active in the same game until Week 8. However, Fleury has maintained the staggering production from Jaxon Smith-Njigba. JSN is just one of four players with 900-plus receiving yards and nine-plus receiving touchdowns in the first eight games of a season in the Super Bowl era (since 1966). The other three are Torry Holt (2003), Steve Smith Sr. (2005) and Cooper Kupp (2021). Both Smith and Kupp went on to win the receiving triple crown in their respective seasons. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Cleveland Browns defensive coordinator Mike RutenbergThere was a lot of doubt that the Cleveland Browns' defense could remain among the league's top-half units following the departures of defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz and sack icon Myles Garrett. However, new defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg has done just that with the NFL's No. 13 scoring defense (21.6 points per game allowed) in 2026. Despite not having Garrett, Cleveland has remained stout in the red zone, allowing a 48% red zone touchdown rate -- tied for the seventh-lowest mark in the league with the Denver Broncos. Remarkably, Rutenberg's unit is top 10 in the NFL in sacks (21, tied for ninth), sack rate (7.4%, tenth) and quarterback pressure rate (38.8%, 10th) without blitzing at a high volume -- the Browns' 28.2% blitz rate is the 12th lowest in the league. Rutenberg has pulled off a Moneyball approach to the pass rush by replacing Garrett in the aggregate: 11 players have at least one sack and four players have at least three sacks. That's a job well done for the surprising 5-3 Browns. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. New York Giants defensive coordinator Dennard WilsonIt would've been easy for Dennard Wilson to feel sorry for himself after Brian Burns went down for the season in Week 3. However, New York has remained afloat with a league-average scoring defense (23.0 points allowed per game, 15th in the NFL). That's largely due to Wilson getting creative with his pressure packages and manufacturing havoc, with the league's third-highest blitz rate (41.9%). Doing so has limited opponents to taking what the defense gives them and checking it down frequently, with the Giants allowing just 6.1 yards per pass attempt, the second-lowest figure in the entire league. That's a job well done for a Giants squad that is the surprise NFC East division leader (4-2-1) through eight weeks. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. New York Giants offensive coordinator Matt NagyLosing Jaxson Dart in Week 2 was a crushing blow. Matt Nagy has made the most of a struggling Jameis Winston and Minnesota Vikings castoff J.J. McCarthy at quarterback, and that has led to his unit producing the league's No. 14 scoring offense (23.3 points per game). The 2026 Giants are the first team since the 2016 New England Patriots to have three different starting quarterbacks win a game before November: Dart, Winston and McCarthy. In their last game out, a 27-21 overtime win at the Houston Texans in Week 7, the Giants had four different players run for a touchdown, marking their first such game since 1950. Nagy is also doing a good job keeping Pro Bowl wide receiver Malik Nabers engaged and involved despite the quarterback carousel: Nabers joined Odell Beckham Jr. as the only players in team history with 100-plus receiving yards in four consecutive games. That's strong work for the NFC East division leaders. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric BieniemyEric Bieniemy returned to Kansas City for his second tour of duty as the Chiefs' offensive coordinator in 2026, and he adapted his offense well with the personnel at his disposal. From 2018 to 2021, Kansas City's offense was built off of Patrick Mahomes' deep passing game to Tyreek Hill and Travis Kelce, but in 2026, the offense is centered around Kenneth Walker III's talents. That's been a mostly successful formula for the 5-2 Chiefs with Walker III ranking third in the league in rushing yards (770), second in yards per carry (5.5) and second in tackles avoided (59). 
Bieniemy needs some help at the trade deadline to truly open up the passing game, but the Chiefs ranking 11th in scoring with a 37-year-old Kelce as the top target represents a job well done. He had Mahomes in position to throw the game-winning touchdown to wide receiver Rashee Rice on Sunday at the Denver Broncos, but a false start penalty by offensive tackle Jaylon Moore nullified the score late. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem MorrisThe San Francisco 49ers are the NFL's No. 1 seed through the first eight weeks of the season, and defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' unit deserves some credit for that. They're the league's No. 6 scoring defense (19.9 points per game), the No. 4 total defense (299.3 total yards per game) and the No. 5 run defense (86.8 rushing yards per game). San Francisco has the ninth-worst average time of possession margin in the NFL, possessing the football two minutes fewer than their opponents on average, and that hasn't affected Morris' unit at all. Much of that figure has to do with the passing game inconsistencies with all of the 49ers' wide receiver injuries, but the 49ers defense just keeps on chugging. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Detroit Lions offensive coordinator Drew PetzingOne could look at new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing putting together the NFL's No. 3 scoring offense (29.0 points per game) and say, "Well, anyone could do that." Detroit has the firepower with Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta and Penei Sewell. That group alone represents 17 trips to the Pro Bowl.Petzing's predecessor, John Morton, lost his job after one season and had his play-calling duties stripped by Dan Campbell entering Week 10. Petzing has thrived at giving Gibbs a chance to shine with David Montgomery no longer in the picture. Gibbs totaled his third 150-yard rushing game of 2026 on Sunday in the 19-15 defeat against the Minnesota Vikings after having just two such games in his first three seasons combined. Petzing also isn't afraid to get creative after having St. Brown line up 10 yards behind Goff on a third-and-8, and the pass play that allowed St. Brown to catch the ball while already moving at near top speed went for a first down against the NFL's No. 1 defense. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Pittsburgh Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham The Pittsburgh Steelers' defense has come back to life under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. They're the league's No. 3 scoring defense (18.0 points per game allowed), No. 6 total defense (305.6 total yards per game allowed), No. 3 run defense (83.9 rushing yards per game allowed), No. 8 third down defense (34.3% third down conversion rate allowed),  No. 2 red zone defense (37.5% third down conversion rate allowed) and tied for No. 3 in takeaways (13). Having All-Pro edge rusher T.J. Watt turning back the clock also helps. After he had just 7.0 sacks in 14 games last season, Watt has 7.5 in eight games this season, which is tied for the league lead with Houston Texans All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. No team has more sacks in the NFL than Graham's unit's 26, one more than the Brian Flores blitzkrieg Minnesota Vikings attack.  The Browns were flying high entering Week 8 with a 5-2 record, but they left Pittsburgh 5-3 after a 27-6 defeat in which the Steelers held them to both season-lows in points (6) and rushing yards (34). Graham is crushing it.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan GannonWhat Jonathan Gannon is doing in his first season as the defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers is nothing short of miraculous. The Packers are 5-3 and would be in the playoffs if the 2026 season ended today despite having fewer than 500 yards rushing.Having the league's worst rushing offense (60.6 rushing yards per game) has heavily contributed to Gannon's defense being on the field for an average time of possession of 31:36, the third highest in the NFL. Micah Parsons isn't expected to return from his torn ACL until Thanksgiving, and top inside linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season with a torn Achilles. Green Bay is a top-10 scoring defense (20.5 points per game allowed) and a top-10 total defense (314.9 total yards per game allowed).  That is remarkable. How has he done it? One might think Gannon is like fellow NFC North defensive mastermind Brian Flores, blitzing all day, every day, to compensate for the lack of Parsons, but that's not the case. The Packers blitz at a 33.4% clip, which ranks 13th in the NFL. Gannon has been able to do it the old-fashioned way by developing some of the Packers' talent that has had more potential than it has produced. Edge rusher Lukas Van Ness, the 13th overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, produced what was a career-high 4.0 sacks as a rookie in 2023.
"Honestly man, JG is not scared. He is not shying away from things because we lost a couple of players. He is still going to dial that shit up you know what I mean?" Packers safety Javon Bullard said after Green Bay's "Thursday Night Football" victory over the Carolina Panthers in Week 8, via NBC 26 in Green Bay. "I think that shows a lot of confidence in the players that we have, and honestly that's huge kudos to him because not a lot of coaches dial it up like that. Not a lot of coaches are as aggressive as he is. I think that's what you want in a coordinator, man. You want a nasty defense. You want a rugged defense. A loud defense. A confident defense. Your coordinator has to damn near replicate that. I think we complement each other real well."With Gannon, Van Ness has a career-high of 4.5 sacks, and the Packers still have nine games left to play. He is also maximizing the talent Green Bay has at safety with All-Pro Xavier McKinney (three interceptions) and Evan Williams (two interceptions and a fumble recovery) each having three takeaways this season, tied for the third most in the NFL. Williams, a 2024 fourth-round pick, is actually the NFL's highest-graded safety with a Pro Football Focus defensive grade of 90.6. description: The Thunder appear ready to move on from Nikola Topić, while the Hornets did not extend a former top-six pick
body:
The Thunder appear ready to move on from Nikola Topić, while the Hornets did not extend a former top-six pick

        Normally, the NBA's deadline for teams to pick up team options on their rookie-scale contracts is Halloween. As the end of October came on a weekend this year, however, it was pushed to Monday. This deadline is usually relatively uneventful. Former first-round picks living up to expectations, or with obvious paths to improvement in the near future, have their third- and fourth-year options picked up. Obvious busts tend not to.Of course, teams inevitably get these decisions wrong from time to time, and that sends promising players to unrestricted free agency at the end of the season in question. The most notable recent example came in 2021, when the Phoenix Suns declined their third-year option on Jalen Smith, whom they'd selected at No. 10 overall ahead of players like Devin Vassell and Tyrese Haliburton less than a year earlier. Smith has since grown into one of the NBA's better shooting big men for the Chicago Bulls.I bring this up because a handful of notable team options were declined ahead of Monday's deadline, setting some interesting prospects up for unrestricted free agency next summer. The NBA is more financially cautious than it has ever been thanks to the aprons, forcing teams to make hard decisions on young players before their futures are fully written. There will inevitably be more Jalen Smiths in the years to come, and a few declined options from the past few days stand out as candidates.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Thunder seemingly giving up on a former lottery pick
There's a degree of validation that comes with being drafted by the Oklahoma City Thunder. Sam Presti thought Nikola Topić was worth the No. 12 overall pick in 2024, and while Presti is hardly infallible, he's the NBA's best general manager by a wide margin and his instincts are usually worth imitation. Oklahoma City didn't decline Topić's 2027-28 option because he's played poorly. They declined it because he's barely played at all.
He missed his rookie season with a torn ACL. He missed most of his second getting treated for testicular cancer, only appearing briefly in 10 games. He has not yet played this season because of back surgery. It is entirely possible that Topić simply never stays healthy enough to reach his potential as a player. It is also entirely possible, especially on a Thunder team that suddenly needs minutes wherever they can find them, that he starts living up to that potential the moment he returns to floor.Oklahoma City's injuries represent the greatest opportunity of Topić's career. The team that drafted him averaged 66 wins in his first two seasons. There weren't going to be many minutes available for him anyway. Now, if he can just make it back onto the court, he should get real on-ball reps for the team with the best player-development track record in basketball. He can set himself up for a real opportunity in unrestricted free agency next summer. The Thunder were never going to be able to afford him long-term considering all of their other obligations, so in that sense, they've arguably done Topić a favor. If they'd picked up his option and then cap dumped him later, he might have wound up in a bad basketball situation. Now, he has the rest of the season to show what he can do and the freedom to shop his services to the teams that need them most.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jazz ready to move on from backup point guard
Guard minutes were readily available for the Utah Jazz over the last two seasons. Isaiah Collier took plenty of them, averaging over 25 minutes per game in each of his first two seasons. Even with Darryn Peterson in the fold this year and Ace Bailey taking on a bigger role next to Keyonte George, Collier has still been featured pretty heavily by backup standards. Case in point: through six games, he is averaging the most minutes on the roster (18.5) of anyone who has not yet started a game.Yet the Jazz surprisingly decided to decline his option for the 2027-28 campaign on Monday. What this means for the Jazz next season still isn't clear. Utah still has plenty of room below next season's projected luxury tax, but that space could evaporate quickly if they elect to re-sign restricted free agent Brice Sensabaugh and/or use a mid-level exception. Perhaps the Jazz want to seek out a veteran backup. They may also prefer to minimize their investment in ball-handlers to ensure that both George and Peterson play on the ball when the other rests. The Jazz have plenty of shot-creation in the front court. They can afford to be stingy at backup point guard.Collier arrived in the NBA as a high-level playmaker. His scoring and defense just haven't kept up. But he was once the No. 1 recruit in his high school class, and there's plenty of tape on him already for other teams to study. The talent is here even if the role potentially wouldn't have been in Utah.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Hornets decline option on former No. 6 pick, but there's a path back
Tidjane Salaün was the highest draft 2024 Draft pick (No. 6 overall) to have his fourth-year option declined, but that probably works in favor of a potential reunion between him and the Charlotte Hornets over the summer if both sides want to pursue one. When a player has a rookie-scale option declined, his original team can still re-sign him in free agency ... but only up to the salary he would have made on that option. Salaün's fourth-year salary would have been $10.4 million or so.That's a much heftier figure than later picks, and it creates a bit of a win-win scenario for the Hornets. If Salaün doesn't live up to that figure, they aren't forced to pay it to him and could try to keep him at a lower rate. If he does, however, then they are at least getting a productive player at a scarce position for this season. If nothing else, that's a valuable trade chip at the deadline.Salaün's overall minutes have gone down in each of his NBA seasons thus far, but he's playing better than he ever has in that smaller role this year. That's not saying all that much, but his combination of physical traits, theoretical ball-handling and shooting and willingness to play hard at least offer the outline of a useful, all-around wing. This is a player archetype that teams are usually eager to take chances on. Whether it's with Charlotte or somebody else, Salaün will probably get another chance.
